g.passage: If Richard prayed, it was with the heart, for his lips never opened. But I believe that his heart, in this hour of clear defeat, was turned to stone. He took his joys with riot, his triumphs calmly; his griefs he shut in a trap. Such a nature as his, I suppose, respects no persons. Whether God beat him, or his enemy, he would take it the same way. All that Gilles heard him say aloud was this: 'What I have done I have done: deliver us from evil.' He bade no farewell to his hope, he asked no greeting for his altered way. When he had turned his back upon the sacred places he lowered his shield; and then rode down the hill into the cold shadow of the valley.

Had Luther stood alone, he, too, would probably have remained silent. What was he, a poor, friendless, solitary monk, that he should set himself against the majesty of the triple crown?

However hateful the walls of a dungeon, a man of sense confined alone there does not dash his hands against the stones.

But Luther knew that his thoughts were the thoughts of thousands. Many wrong things, as we all know, have to be endured in this world. Authority is never very angelic; and moderate injustice, a moderate quantity of lies, is more tolerable than anarchy.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Measured and realistic
Furious and rebellious
Mocking and dismissive
Joyful and carefree
g.explanation: 글쓴이는 Luther가 혼자였다면 침묵했을 것이라며 감옥 벽에 손을 부딪치지 않는 분별 있는 사람을 예로 든다. 또 적당한 불의가 무정부보다 견딜 만하다고 차분히 말한다. B와 C는 이런 절제된 태도와 맞지 않고, D는 주제의 무게와 어긋난다. 따라서 정답은 A이다.

g.passage: For a long time we followed the pathway of an avalanche. To the right and left of us, upon considerable heights, the trees were sound and whole, and preserved, even at their ripe age, the health of youth. But down the straight pathway of the valley every tree had been swept away, the prostrate trunks, lying here and there, half buried in drifts of sand and rock. Here, over the whole surface, a fresh young growth not more than six or seven years old has sprung up, and begun a hopeless struggle for ground which the snow claims for its own. Before us opened winding avenues through forest; green meadows spread their pale, fresh herbage in sunny beauty.

g.explanation: 화자는 눈사태 길에 쓰러진 나무와 양옆의 건강한 나무를 자세히 대조한다. 또 어린 숲이 '희망 없는 싸움'을 시작했다고 담담히 생각한다. A, C, D는 이런 차분한 관찰과 맞지 않는다. 따라서 정답은 B이다.

g.passage: A thousand German colonists were called in and settled on the heath, but it was stronger than they, and they drifted away until scarce half a hundred families remained. The Government tried its hand, but there was no one who knew just how, and only discouragement resulted. Then came the war with Germany in 1864, that lost to Denmark a third of her territory. The country lay prostrate under the crushing blow. But it rose above defeat and disaster, and once more expectant eyes were turned toward the ancient domain that had slipped from its grasp.
g.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Denmark and the heath?
options: The heath was quickly tamed by the first German colonists.
The Danish government cared nothing for the ancient heath.
The heath defeated settlers, yet Denmark later looked to it again.
The war with Germany made Denmark give up on the heath forever.
g.explanation: 황야는 독일 정착민들보다 '강해서' 그들이 떠나갔고 정부의 시도도 실패했다. 그러나 패전 뒤 덴마크는 다시 기대에 찬 눈으로 그 땅을 바라본다. A는 정착 실패와 반대이고, B는 정부가 시도했다는 말과 어긋나며, D는 다시 관심을 둔다는 결말과 반대이다. 따라서 정답은 C이다.

g.passage:
Almost without exception, it is by way of passion that a man and a woman approach each other. It is, of necessity, the exterior that first comes into view. Thus, all that youth and inexperience can know about love is its aspect of passion. Because Jane had again and again in her five grown-up years experienced men falling passionately in love with her, she fancied she was an expert in matters of love. In fact, she had still everything to learn.

On the way home she, assuming that the affair was as good as settled, that she and Victor Dorn were lovers, was busy with plans for the future.
g.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes Jane's view of her relationship with Victor Dorn?
options: Jane and Victor have openly agreed to marry very soon.
Jane distrusts Victor because he resembles her past admirers.
Victor has been chasing Jane passionately for five years.
Jane assumes a settled bond with Victor that may not exist.
g.explanation: 서술자는 Jane이 연애 전문가라고 착각하지만 '아직 모든 것을 배워야 한다'고 말한다. 그런 그녀가 일이 거의 정해졌다고 '가정하며' Victor와의 미래를 계획한다. A는 확정된 합의가 없어 틀리고, B와 C는 지문에 없는 내용이다. 따라서 정답은 D이다.

g.passage:
Simple, natural, mild, and gracious, the gentle reserve of his manner added, under the circumstances, to the interest which he inspired. Somewhat of that reserve continued even after our acquaintance had ripened into intimacy.

He never spoke of his own past history, or future prospects, shunned all political discourse, and was with difficulty drawn into conversation upon the scenery and manners of the North of Europe. He seemed afraid of the subject.

Upon general topics, whether of literature or art, he was remarkably open and candid. He possessed in an eminent degree the talent of acquiring languages for which his countrymen are distinguished, and had made the best use of those keys of knowledge.
g.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the narrator's relationship with the man?
options: They grew close, though he stayed guarded about his past.
They argued often about politics and life in the North.
He openly told the narrator his entire life history.
The narrator found him rude and ended the acquaintance.
g.explanation: 두 사람의 친분은 '친밀함으로 무르익었지만' 그의 조심스러움은 계속되었다. 그는 자신의 과거나 미래, 정치 이야기를 피했다. B는 그가 정치 이야기를 피했다는 말과 반대이고, C는 과거를 말하지 않았다는 점과 어긋나며, D는 그의 온화한 태도와 맞지 않는다. 따라서 정답은 A이다.

g.passage: I feel much obliged by your kind proposition as regards myself. For the present I must remain where I am. When I see that I have done all the good that I can accomplish for Washington College I may find it necessary to do something that will enable me to procure a competence for my family. I will then turn my hand to whatever may offer. For myself I want nothing but my food and clothes. I send in compliance with your request a number of autographs, enough, I should think, to last for all time; but if they will be of any service to you I will send more.

options: The writer resents the recipient for asking him for autographs.
